label: Conspiracy that was TRUE

szenen.text: In 1950, the U.S. Navy sprayed bacteria over *San Francisco.*
Nobody was told. Residents were *test subjects.*
The microbe was *Serratia marcescens.* Officials thought it was harmless.
Days later, patients at a Stanford hospital got *sick.*
Eleven were infected. One patient, Edward Nevin, *died.*
The tests became public in the *1970s.*
The Nevin family sued in 1981. The case was *dismissed.*
Should citizens be told *first?* Follow for more.
